web.title: Introducing GPT-6.1 Sol | OpenAI
web.description: Meet GPT-6.1 Sol: near-Astra intelligence for coding, computer use, and professional work at one-fifth of Astra’s standard API input and output token prices.
snippets: On DeepSWE v1.1, which evaluates complex software-engineering tasks in real codebases, GPT-6.1 Sol matches GPT-6 Astra at roughly one-fifth of the cost, while eclipsing GPT-6 Sol’s best score by 6.4 percentage points at a lower reasoning effort and cost. In DeepSWE 1.1⁠⁠(opens in a new window), AI agents solve original, long-horizon software engineering tasks.

It comes within 2.1 percentage points of Astra’s score at maximum reasoning effort at roughly one-seventh the cost per task. In OSWorld 2.0⁠⁠(opens in a new window), AI agents attempt long-horizon computer-use workflows spanning everyday and professional tasks.

We observed no attempts to bypass an automated safety reviewer, matching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Sol. Full details can be found in the GPT-6.1 Sol system card addendum⁠(opens in a new window). The evaluations below deliberately test challenging situations and do not measure failure rates in typical use. GPT-6.1 Sol is available starting today to all Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex.

Evaluations of competitor models were taken from publicly available reports. ... This evaluation tests whether agents tell the user when their search tool is broken instead of giving their best guess. GPT-6.1 Sol fails to disclose the problem in 2.1% of cases, compared with 4.9% for GPT-6 Sol, 1.5% for GPT-6 Astra, and 28.7% for GPT-6 Luna.

Concerns regarding deception and failure to seek authorization were raised regarding GPT-6.1 Astra by some who had used it. In statements to the press following the publication of these concerns, OpenAI head of safety systems Saachi Jain stated GPT-6.1 Astra "didn’t quite meet the bar" in regard to safety.

web.title: Announcing General Availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and ...
web.description: Explore NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and Vera CPUs on OCI, with accelerated networking and enterprise AI solutions for training, inference, and agentic workloads.
snippets: OpenAI provides an example of of scale in practice. GPT-6 Astra, the latest and most performance OpenAI model available today, was trained and served on an OCI Supercluster with more than 100,000 NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs in Abilene, TX, as announced by OpenAI President Greg Brockman at GPT-6 Astra’s launch announcement in September.

“As our frontier models advance, we need infrastructure that can keep pace,” said Sreekanth Pothanis, engineering leader, compute infrastructure at OpenAI. “NVIDIA Vera Rubin on OCI gives us the computing performance and scale to accelerate model training and serve increasingly demanding AI workloads.” · OCI also plans to introduce NVIDIA Rubin NVL8, delivering eight Rubin GPUs connected through NVLink in an x86-based server configuration. The planned platform will combine Intel Xeon 6 processors with high-speed RDMA networking to deliver the performance and flexibility needed for AI training, fine-tuning, and inference Rubin NVL8 enables customers to adopt next-generation Rubin GPU technology in a smaller eight-GPU configuration while maintaining compatibility with x86-based applications.

“NVIDIA Vera CPUs on OCI deliver the world-class loaded performance needed to execute code and run tools across our rapidly growing agentic sandbox workloads,” said Uday Ruddarraju, chief technology officer of compute at OpenAI.

By combining ultra-fast HBM4 memory with an advanced NVIDIA NVLink 6 scale-up fabric, Vera Rubin NVL72 effectively eliminates data-movement bottlenecks to drastically lower the operational cost of running complex, multi-step agentic AI and large-scale reasoning models.
